CoverageModel: Every production CheckId is assigned exactly one reusable risk profile; narrow per-check overrides carry exceptional severity, risk or relationships.

Profiles.Name: inventory-context
Profiles.Description: Resolves the provider, tenant, host or asset scope needed for a trustworthy assessment.
Profiles.Risk: Missing or partial context creates blind spots, invalid comparisons and false confidence in audit coverage.
Profiles.Remediation: Restore least-privilege read access, verify the selected scope and rerun before treating the report as authoritative.

Profiles.Name: scope-governance
Profiles.Description: Constrains assessment targets to explicit, authorized scope.
Profiles.Risk: An implicit or malformed scope can test unauthorized assets or omit assets that the operator intended to assess.
Profiles.Remediation: Declare exact authorized targets, review the scope plan and rerun without wildcards or inferred assets.

Profiles.Name: identity-access
Profiles.Description: Evaluates authentication strength, credential lifecycle and privilege boundaries.
Profiles.Risk: Weak authentication or excessive privilege can allow account takeover, persistent administrative access and cross-service compromise.
Profiles.Remediation: Enforce phishing-resistant authentication, remove standing privilege and replace long-lived credentials with managed short-lived identities.

Profiles.Name: logging-detection
Profiles.Description: Evaluates telemetry collection, security detections and evidence availability.
Profiles.Risk: Missing telemetry delays detection, prevents reliable investigation and lets malicious activity blend into normal operations.
Profiles.Remediation: Enable the native audit source, centralize protected retention and verify that the SOC can query representative events.

Profiles.Name: data-protection
Profiles.Description: Evaluates public access, encryption, retention and sharing controls around cloud data.
Profiles.Risk: Weak data controls can expose sensitive content, enable destructive changes or prevent recovery and legal retention.
Profiles.Remediation: Remove unintended public access, enforce encryption and apply retention and sharing policy at the broadest safe scope.

Profiles.Name: network-security
Profiles.Description: Evaluates DNS, routing, listener, firewall and overlay-network trust boundaries.
Profiles.Risk: Uncontrolled exposure or broken naming and trust boundaries can enable takeover, unauthorized access and lateral movement.
Profiles.Remediation: Restrict exposure to explicit sources and services, remove stale references and validate layered network enforcement.

Profiles.Name: email-security
Profiles.Description: Evaluates mail authentication, forwarding and legacy protocol controls.
Profiles.Risk: Weak mail controls enable spoofing, credential phishing, covert forwarding and abuse of legacy authentication paths.
Profiles.Remediation: Enforce SPF, DKIM and DMARC, block unintended forwarding and disable legacy mail protocols unless explicitly required.

Profiles.Name: platform-hardening
Profiles.Description: Evaluates operating-system hardening and patch hygiene.
Profiles.Risk: Unpatched or weakly hardened hosts increase exploitability and give attackers durable local persistence.
Profiles.Remediation: Apply security updates within the maintenance policy and verify host controls after reboot or configuration reload.

Overrides.Risk: Compromise of an AWS root identity without MFA gives an attacker unrestricted account control, including billing, identity and destructive actions.
Overrides.Remediation: Enable hardware or FIDO2 MFA for root, remove root access keys and use IAM Identity Center for administrative work.

Overrides.Risk: A privileged identity outside effective MFA coverage can be used to seize the tenant and weaken downstream controls.
Overrides.Remediation: Require phishing-resistant MFA for every privileged role, validate Conditional Access coverage and tightly govern break-glass exclusions.

Overrides.Risk: An allow-all tailnet rule collapses segmentation and can turn one compromised identity or device into broad lateral access.
Overrides.Remediation: Replace allow-all rules with reviewed groups, tags and explicit destination services; test policy before deployment.

Overrides.Risk: A dangling CNAME can let an attacker claim the external service and serve trusted content or phishing from the organization domain.
Overrides.Remediation: Remove the stale CNAME or reclaim the referenced service, then verify DNS and HTTP behavior before closing the finding.
